transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-16
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendoza (Redwood SE), Jared Collins (OmniBank CISO), Priya Nair (OmniBank Head of Infra), Liam O'Connor (OmniBank Sr Eng)

Summary: quick security review focused on encryption at-rest and in-transit, KMS integration options (BYOK vs Redwood-managed), HSM/KMIP support, audit logging and data residency questions. Customer wants BYOK with HSM-backed keys for hosted inference, possible Private deployment if needed.

00:00 Samantha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, im Samantha from Redwood AE, and Carlos our SE will run through technical details. Jared, Priya, Liam, thanks for making time.
00:23 Jared: Yeah thanks, uh quick background — OmniBank is rolling LLM features into fraud ops, need to make sure keys never leave our control, lots of compliance, PCI scoping, so encryption is, like, table stakes.
00:35 Carlos: Got it. We'll go through our envelope encryption model, BYOK flow, and HSM options. quick note, some of my wording may be a little informal, apologies for typos in the transcript, etc.
01:05 Priya: Important for us: we need FIPS 140-2 / 140-3 certified HSM support, key separation, and audit logs that show key usage. Also data residency — EU for EU customers.
01:30 Carlos: Understood. For hosted Redwood we do envelope encryption: customer-provided key (BYOK) in your KMS wraps a data key; Redwood uses the wrapped key to encrypt model cache and ephemeral KV, we never see plaintext KEKs. There are two models — BYOK with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) or HSM-backed keys via CloudHSM or customer HSM for Private installs.
02:10 Liam: quick question — when you say you never see plaintext KEK, do you mean the key material is never in Redwood process memory, or is it unwrapped inside the service for a short time?
02:28 Carlos: Good question. For hosted envelope flow we unwrap inside a secure enclave on the node for a minimal window; we try to keep it in an ephemeral memory region and it gets torn down per lifecycle. If customers require the key never be unwrapped on Redwood-managed hosts, we recommend Private deployment pointing at your HSM/KMS or an EKM arrangement. Apologies if that was fuzzy.
03:05 Jared: Ok. So our compliance team prefers HSM-backed keys and no plaintext ever on vendor memory. That would push us toward Private or a dedicated VPC pattern?
03:20 Samantha: Right — there are gradations. Hosted + BYOK with envelope encryption is acceptable to some banks if the unwrapping window and audit controls are documented. But for highest assurance — HSM where customer controls the key lifecycle and the vendor never has the unwrapped key — Private (or Dedicated with HSM integration) is the safer choice.
03:51 Priya: What's the integration surface? do you support KMIP or PKCS#11 or CloudHSM API?
04:05 Carlos: We support Cloud provider KMS APIs (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) out of the box. For HSMs there are two main patterns: 1) for Private installs we can integrate with customer HSMs over PKCS#11 or KMIP depending on vendor, 2) for cloud HSMs like AWS CloudHSM, we can integrate via EKM or through a KMS which holds the HSM-protected keys. We also have customers using Thales/HSM via KMIP gateways.
04:40 Liam: If we choose hosted + BYOK, how do rotations work? we rotate keys in our KMS, what does Redwood need?
04:52 Carlos: We follow an envelope pattern: when you rotate the wrapping key in your KMS you provide a new wrapped data key; Redwood stores the wrapped keys and will use the active wrapping key to unwrap. We also support key-version metadata so older data is rewrapped lazily or on next write. We'll send the rotation checklist.
05:20 Jared: Audit logs — we need proof of who requested keys and when. Does Redwood surface KMS access logs or key use events in your console?
05:35 Samantha: Yes, we provide per-request audit logs in the Console and can export to your SIEM. For hosted BYOK we log key unwrap events, the Redwood node ID, timestamp, and the request ID. For Private, you control KMS audit logs entirely. Note: some cloud KMS providers redact certain fields; we can correlate logs with our traces.
06:05 Priya: Are logs tamper-evident and retained for at least a year?
06:12 Carlos: We provide immutable append-only logs in our observability pipeline and can set retention to customer requirements for enterprise tiers. For highest assurance we recommend shipping logs to your own SIEM/Log archive.
06:32 Liam: What about encryption in transit between our app and Redwood and between nodes?
06:38 Samantha: All control-plane and data-plane traffic is TLS 1.2/1.3. For cross-region traffic we also support mTLS between nodes. Keys in transit are ephemeral and encrypted.
06:55 Jared: Another question: can we do key attestation or certify the HSM version? Our auditors ask for FIPS cert numbers.
07:05 Carlos: Yes, for Private deployments we can document the HSM vendor and FIPS level — e.g., CloudHSM v2 (FIPS 140-2) or Thales Luna series. We'll capture model and firmware versions. For hosted, cloud KMS attestation is provided by the cloud provider; we can surface their attestation doc.
07:40 Priya: For PCI and some of our regs, the key custodianship and separation of duties is required. Does Redwood have RBAC tied to key operations?
07:52 Samantha: On the Redwood Console we have RBAC controls and SSO (SAML/OIDC). We can limit who triggers key unwrap flows and who can modify KMS config. We also provide role-based audit trails. For extra controls you can gate KMS key policies to require certain principal or approval.
08:20 Jared: Does Redwood support HSM-backed signing for logs or attestation?
08:28 Carlos: Not natively for logs, but many customers use their HSM to sign manifests or aggregated hashes exported from Redwood. We can add an export pipeline that produces signed manifests for your auditors.
08:52 Priya: If we need guaranteed zero-knowledge keys (never unwrapped on vendor nodes), can you run tokenization where the model calls are proxied through our network?
09:03 Carlos: There are two options: Private deployment inside your VPC (best), or Dedicated nodes with network peering + EKM. For hosted we can't guarantee never unwrapped unless the HSM provider supports remote key operations without key material leaving their enclave and our integration uses EKM-style APIs. It's vendor-specific.
09:35 Liam: ok, what's the effort to do a PoC to validate BYOK with our CloudHSM?
09:42 Samantha: usually 2-4 weeks: onboarding, test keys, basic encryption/decryption flows, some perf tests. Carlos will own technical steps. We'll schedule a PoC kickoff.
10:05 Jared: On the legal side, we need a data processing addendum and contract language about key custody and breach notification. We'll loop in legal after this.
10:18 Samantha: We'll share standard DPA and propose clauses; legal folks have used our SSO and DPA before.
10:30 (timestamp noise) Speaker 3: mm-hmm...
10:45 Carlos: Next I'll run a quick technical deep dive — apologies if i jump into details.
11:10 Carlos: Tech note: our runtime stores model weights and KV cache on disk encrypted with a per-instance data key; that data key is encrypted (wrapped) with the customer KEK provided by KMS. For inference we decrypt only the needed ephemeral payloads. We also support in-memory encryption for swap.
11:45 Liam: So for latency-sensitive paths, does unwrapping add much overhead?
11:52 Carlos: Minimal — unwrap is an API call to your KMS, usually sub-100ms for cloud KMS, but we cache data keys and reuse them per lifecycle to avoid per-request unwraps. For very strict controls where unwraps must be logged per inference, that's configurable but will add cost/latency.
12:25 Priya: We need per-token auditability for some flows; can that be done?
12:31 Carlos: Not per-token key unwrap, but you can log inference request IDs and correlate with key-use events; per-token unwrap is generally impractical. We'll discuss options in the PoC.
13:00 Jared: On BRD, our security bar requires HSM-backed keys and key rotation every 90 days. Does Redwood support automated rotation?
13:12 Carlos: Yes, we support rotation workflows. If you rotate wrapping keys in KMS, provide the new wrapped key and set it active; Redwood honors rotation metadata and can rewrap lazily or trigger a background rewrap process. We'll document the exact steps.
13:40 Priya: Regarding key export — we must ensure Redwood can't export unwrapped keys. Is that in your threat model?
13:48 Samantha: Yes — for hosted BYOK we ensure we never persist plaintext KEK; wrapped keys are stored. For Private, keys live in your HSM. We'll add language to the threat model docs and share.
14:10 Liam: Are there any known limitations with Azure Key Vault or GCP KMS? we use multi-cloud.
14:18 Carlos: Mostly parity across providers, but differences in key wrapping algorithm support and key sizes. We'll include a matrix. Also note some providers limit allowed key operations or rate limits; we'll need to test under load.
14:45 Jared: Rate limits are a concern. If we have a batch of inference requests, will KMS API throttling be a bottleneck?
14:55 Carlos: That's why we cache unwrapped data keys and only call KMS for rotation/unwrap events. For designs that require strict per-request unwrap we recommend a local key cache with audited access or Private deployment.
15:20 Priya: For HSM based on-prem, are there deployment docs?
15:25 Samantha: Yes — we'll share our Private deployment guide and KMS integration appendix. It lists PKCS#11 endpoints, KMIP configs, firewall rules, and test vectors.
15:45 Liam: Can you support PKCS#11 v3 and dynamic slot mapping?
15:51 Carlos: We have customers using PKCS#11 v2/3; we'll validate with your vendor. Sometimes middleware is needed.
16:10 Jared: About key lifecycle: If we decommission a key, how do you handle existing encrypted objects?
16:18 Carlos: Best practice is to rotate to a new key and keep old wrapped keys until data is re-encrypted or retired. If a KEK is destroyed, you lose access to NP (encrypted artifacts). We recommend archival policies and key backup.
16:44 Priya: Data residency — can we pin customer data to EU-only nodes while using Redwood hosted?
16:51 Samantha: Yes, per-region routing can keep inference in EU regions; however KMS integration must be in the same region for lowest latency; we can also set routing policy to force EU-only.
17:15 Liam: Will you share a sample of the audit logs format?
17:20 Carlos: Yes — we'll attach a sample JSON schema showing fields like timestamp, action, principal_id, node_id, request_id, key_id, operation.
17:40 Jared: What about encryption of model weights at rest in S3? who manages the SSE-C or SSE-KMS?
17:50 Carlos: If using hosted object storage we use SSE-KMS with your KMS wrapping the S3 encryption key. For Private you control the S3 or object store and its key management. There can be cross-account roles for AWS.
18:18 Priya: For HSM certificate management, we need to ensure firmware patches and key rotation windows are documented.
18:26 Carlos: We'll provide recommended maintenance windows and patch cadence in the runbook.
18:45 Samantha: Quick note — some transcription glitches might have mangled acronyms here and there, sorry.
19:00 Jared: Okay, two blocker items: must have HSM-backed keys with attestable FIPS level, and legal needs explicit DPA clause for key custody. If hosted can't meet these, we'll evaluate Private.
19:20 Samantha: Understood. We'll prioritize the HSM attestation and DPA.
19:35 Priya: Could you also confirm whether Redwood stores any unencrypted logs that might contain sensitive prompts or PII?
19:45 Carlos: By default we redact sensitive prompt content in logs for hosted customers; for enterprise tiers we can configure retention and redaction policies. We'll send our log retention and redaction guide.
20:10 Liam: On the performance side, can we have a quick benchmark for unwrap latency with CloudHSM?
20:18 Carlos: Yes, part of PoC we'll run unwrap/rewrap throughput and end-to-end latency tests.
20:40 Jared: Are there recommended KMS policies we should set to restrict unwraps to Redwood service principals?
20:48 Samantha: Yes, we'll provide a policy snippet that limits key use to specific IAM roles and conditions like source IP or VPC. We'll include examples for AWS/IAM and Azure Managed Identities.
21:10 Priya: Any concerns about secret scoping in your codebase? we need to know what secrets are stored where.
21:18 Carlos: We treat all customer keys as sensitive; we store only wrapped keys and metadata. Access to secrets in Redwood org is RBAC controlled and logged. We'll provide an inventory of where wrapped keys and metadata are stored.
21:45 Jared: For the PoC, we want Redwood to integrate with our CloudHSM in eu-west-1 and prove that the HSM-backed KEK never leaves the HSM. Can you do a live demo?
21:58 Samantha: Yes, demo + PoC. We'll need IAM roles, KMIP endpoints, and a test key. We'll coordinate offline.
22:20 (short chatter) Speaker 4: uh yeah
22:35 Carlos: I'll put together the technical checklist: key import vs key generation, wrapping algorithm (RSA-OAEP/AES-GCM), allowed key sizes, rotation cadence, api endpoints for unwrap/wrap.
23:05 Priya: Also share your incident response playbook for key compromise scenarios.
23:12 Samantha: Will do.
23:30 Jared: Last question: for multi-tenant use, how do you ensure logical separation of keys?
23:38 Carlos: Customer isolation is enforced at the tenant layer; keys are namespaced per-tenant and access requires tenant-scoped credentials. For Dedicated/Private we have stronger isolation since infra is separate.
24:00 Liam: Is there a cost delta for BYOK/HSM integration?
24:06 Samantha: There can be additional costs for Private or Dedicated with HSM integration (setup, ongoing maintenance). We'll include pricing options.
24:30 Jared: Great. Let's recap next steps.
24:35 Samantha: Recap: 1) Samantha to send SOC2/ISO and DPA template; 2) Carlos to send BYOK integration checklist + sample audit log schema; 3) Customer to confirm HSM vendor and region; 4) Schedule PoC kickoff (2-4 week timeline).
24:55 Jared: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
25:05 Priya: Thanks.
25:10 (call ends)

Notes: transcript has small transcription errors (e.g., acronyms), timestamps roughly every 30-90 seconds. Links/resources mentioned to be attached: /security/soc2.pdf, /security/bYOK-checklist.md, sample-audit-log-schema.json.
